notes: Fixed the single-use port errors: the MKR ENV Shield is now joined to the MKR WiFi 1010 only through env1:MKR.socket. The jumper wires go to the board's pins (D2-D5, GND), which the shield's headers pass through. I removed the pin-by-pin pass-through edges.

Fixed the resistor count: the parts list has a single '220 ohm' resistor, so r1 is the only one and r2-r4 are removed. I did not give each LED channel its own resistor. Both LED cathodes (white LED and RGB common cathode) go to one shared breadboard strip (column 25), and r1 sits between that strip and the ground rail. That way every LED still has a series current limit with only one resistor. A shared resistor means brightness varies with how many channels are on.
The schematic image was not visible, so the wiring follows the sketch's pin defines: pin 5 is the white LED, pin 2 is RGB red, pin 3 is RGB blue and pin 4 is RGB green.
The MKR ENV Shield (new type, because lookup_part found nothing for it) is stacked on the MKR WiFi 1010. Its temperature sensor is read over internal I2C, which is not drawn as a separate edge.
The breadboard holes used are my own layout choice. The jumper wire count (7) is an assumption.
